subject: shore landforms
defect: Repeated grassy domes with steep smooth gray rock skirts lack layered shore ecology and clear grass-to-sand transitions
notes: Confirmed across four seeded route/off-route frames; gray rock skirts and abrupt green tops are visible at near and far range.

subject: creature hurt and movement poses
defect: Hurt and moving frames often retain the idle silhouette so the state is difficult to read without a filename
notes: Still frames cannot establish locomotion timing; check production transition captures before scheduling animation work. Tidewake and Stormwood stills confirm the recurring state-read gap; judge motion before assigning animation timing.

subject: map
defect: The map canvas shows headings and markers without visible terrain or road context for the displayed destinations
notes: First Shore is marked discovered but the Day 1 state may hide survey detail; both biome maps lack terrain/route context at this state.

subject: shiny creature finish
defect: Several shiny variants become near-uniform hot magenta and lose their ordinary species material and pattern identity
notes: Variants are easy to identify; Ripplet and Mosshell retain more form detail.

subject: Veilfall silhouette
defect: The distant Veilfall mountain reads as a near-geometric dark cone with narrow broken waterfall streaks
notes: The near cascade has a broad white curtain and mist in the route frame; limit this defect to far silhouette and landmark legibility.

subject: named destination read
defect: Several named route destinations read as unmarked grassy slopes or small generic structures instead of distinct halls arches or terraces
notes: Seeded route proxy corroborates generic location stands; reshoot true authored route before assigning site work. The Gull Rest tower itself remains a visible local marker.

subject: creature faint state
defect: Several fainted aquatic creatures keep raised alert heads or upright crouches instead of reading as defeated
notes: Mirejaw and Mangrove Monitor show stronger contrasting collapses; validate in a real encounter.

subject: menu shell
defect: The full-screen charcoal menu with thin teal borders has little visual hierarchy or scenic connection to the illustrated world
notes: Same full-screen shell in Meadows and Tidewake production UI; assess Cloudreach and Stormwood before final shared exposure.

subject: secondary menu panels
defect: The Quests Build and Players panels leave most of their area empty around a few plain text lines or a single button
notes: The Day 1 fixture may explain empty panels, but the screen leaves large dead areas. Skills capture still resembles Quests; verify navigation.

subject: water and island depth
defect: Broad offshore water reads as uniform light cyan with little depth variation across several island routes
notes: Brine Steps shore has strong foam and wave detail; this row concerns open-water distance views only.

subject: exploration HUD
defect: The many dark boxed HUD panels and outlined text occupy a large share of the exploration view
notes: Tidewake exterior confirms the large team strip quest box quick bar and shortcut bar; Meadows frame is indoors.

subject: Veilfall approach shallows
defect: A ruler-straight chain of nearly identical tan discs with white rims makes the Veilfall approach read as mechanical stepping stones rather than natural current shallows
notes: Recurring from three route views; the thin white water marks reinforce the straight disc chain.

subject: settings and binding instructions
defect: Dense gray-on-navy control instructions and literal key labels make settings and quick binding text hard to scan
notes: Shared menu presentation in two biomes; [Minus] and [Equal] labels are visible in map instructions.

subject: map active region
defect: The Tidewake map title and First Shore discovery are shown while the Meadows region button appears selected and Tidewake appears inactive
notes: Could be Day 1 fixture navigation state rather than product selection behavior; verify after explicitly selecting Tidewake.

subject: creature rest poses
defect: Riptusk and Torrentoad resting poses roll onto their backs with limbs raised and read as distressed rather than settled
notes: Grass obscures contact edges; no floating conclusion from these frames.
